- Assessment:  
  - Adult female with a 3-day history of worsening, severe right-sided headache rated 8/10, characterized as dull with episodes of sharpness  
  - Associated symptoms include transient visual phenomena (shooting lights), photophobia, nausea without vomiting, no neck stiffness, no neurological deficits, difficulty focusing related to headache  
  - Family history notable for migraines in mother and sister  
  - Previous headaches usually responsive to Ibuprofen, current episode refractory to treatment possibly due to inadequate dosing  
- DDx consistent with transcript:  
  - Migraine with aura (High likelihood): supported by severe unilateral headache, photophobia, visual aura, nausea, positive family history, and previous response to NSAIDs  
  - Cluster headache (Moderate likelihood): unilateral eye pain with severe intensity and photophobia, but absence of autonomic features and longer duration make less likely  
  - Tension-type headache (Low to Moderate likelihood): dull headache and work-related stress present but severity and associated symptoms atypical  
- DDx less consistent or contradicted:  
  - Meningitis/encephalitis unlikely: no fever, neck stiffness, or systemic features  
  - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension unlikely: no papilledema, vision loss, or headache pattern consistent  
  - Other diagnoses such as sinusitis, brain tumor, medication overuse headache not supported by history or exam  
- Conflict noted: None  

Management Plan  
- Advise proper dosing of Ibuprofen (up to 2 tablets three times daily)  
- Consider stronger analgesics: prescribe Naproxen and/or paracetamol; codeine may be considered as per patient’s report of maternal use (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
- Recommend headache diary to identify possible triggers  
- Suggest follow-up in 1–2 weeks to reassess frequency and severity; discuss prophylactic treatment if headaches become recurrent  
- Urge patient to seek earlier care if new neurological symptoms develop or headache worsens significantly  
- Recommend an eye exam due to prolonged screen use and visual symptoms  
- Lifestyle advice regarding hydration and stress management as appropriate  
- No investigations or referrals ordered at this time but may be considered if symptoms persist or worsen
